title: Provider payment cuts in CMS’s estimates
alt: Horizontal bar chart of CMS’s central estimates for 2026–2035: the SDP rule cuts provider payments by $774.8 billion; the provider tax rule measured alone cuts $384.0 billion, of which $241.9 billion is already counted in the SDP rule and $142.1 billion is additional; both rules combined cut $916.9 billion.

title: The provider tax rule’s net effect on providers
alt: Waterfall chart: measured alone, the provider tax rule leaves providers $220.3 billion worse off (CMS Table 12); adding back the $241.9 billion overlap already counted in the SDP rule gives CMS’s +$21.7 billion on top of the SDP rule (Table 14).

title: Parts of the two proposed rules that reach each state
alt: Tile map of the 50 states and DC sorted into five groups: 24 states where both rules reach (A), 2 where the cap and a lower threshold on non-hospital taxes reach (B), 3 cap only (C), 8 non-expansion states with SDPs above the caps (D) and 14 with no identified hospital SDPs above the caps (E), five of which the lower threshold reaches; it shows where the rules apply, not where losses are largest.

title: Change in hospital inpatient units
alt: Bar chart from one national study: from 2008 to 2022, pediatric inpatient units fell 29.9 percent and adult inpatient units fell 4.4 percent.

title: Psychiatric beds per 100,000 people, by hospital type
alt: Slope chart of psychiatric beds per 100,000 people from 2011 to 2023: short-term acute care hospitals fell from 11.3 to 9.06, freestanding psychiatric hospitals rose from 16.8 to 19.5, and the total was about flat at 28.1 and 28.4.
